review_limits: No paper draft was supplied; claims-vs-code review was limited to checking consistency between MATCHING/score_tgt_links.do, LINKAGE/code/01_abe_jw/linkage_analysis.do, CODE/create_figures_SSHA2025.do, and the markdown report written by the script.
External .dta datasets on D:/SNU ECON Dropbox/... and F:/... could not be read and Stata was not executed; runtime behavior was verified by static inspection of the source code.
structured_output.summary: MATCHING/score_tgt_links.do faithfully implements the sample definitions, link filtering, two-sided truth classification, recall, and middle-initial validation of LINKAGE/code/01_abe_jw/linkage_analysis.do across all, target, and non-target 1940 records. All Round 1 issues have been resolved: truth file cardinality and one-to-one uniqueness are asserted, the replication gate verifies both main-table and truth-based (V/U/C and recall) benchmarks for ans and true before writing output, pairwise ml-vs-true comparisons are reported both unfiltered and on the 51.0M sample, and the middle-initial block cleanly computes both own-initial and fixed Ancestry-initial validation rates. No defects were found.

verified_clean.evidence: MATCHING/score_tgt_links.do:205-224 merges 1930 middle initials (cn1930) and renames histid1940 to histid before preserve (line 209), computes own-initial validation using mi_v_`c' inside the preserved block, restores to the pre-1940-merge state (line 216) where histid (1940) and mi1930 are already in memory, and merges mi_anc from cn1940_`s' (line 219) with non-empty string guards (mi1930 != "" & mi1940 != "" at line 212 and mi1930 != "" & mi_anc != "" at line 220).
verified_clean.item: Preserve/restore state and merge sequence in the Part 1 middle-initial validation block

verified_clean.evidence: MATCHING/score_tgt_links.do:46-78, 144-146, and 234-270 assert _N==36690338 and one-to-one uniqueness (isid histid1930, isid histid1940) on mlp_training1930_1940.dta, check N_*, nv_*, rate_*, sv_*, ver_*, unv_*, con_*, and recall_* for ans and true on full and restr against the main-table and slide-table benchmarks, and exit with code 9 before opening the output file if any check fails.

summary.description: Two to four sentences. The overall state of the reviewed work and the single most important thing to fix. No preamble.

dimensions_reviewed.description: Which scope dimensions were actually reviewed in this run.

findings.description: Defects and concerns, ordered most severe first. Empty if none. Do not pad with stylistic observations.

severity.description: blocker: a reported result is wrong. major: a referee would demand it. minor: real but survivable. nit: cosmetic.

confidence.description: verified: traced in the source. likely: strongly implied but depends on unseen data. speculative: a question, not an established defect.

title.description: One line, stating the defect itself, not its category.

location.description: path:line, or path:line-line. Several may be comma-separated. Required: a finding without a location is not a finding.

what_the_code_does.description: Precisely what the code computes, quoting the relevant expression. Contrast with what it was evidently intended to compute.

why_it_matters.description: The consequence for a number or claim in the paper. If there is no consequence, the severity is nit.

how_to_check.description: A concrete command, tabulation, or count the author can run to confirm or refute this in minutes.

suggested_fix.description: The change, specific enough to act on. Do not apply it yourself.

verified_clean.description: Things explicitly checked that were fine. This is what makes a short findings list trustworthy rather than lazy.

evidence.description: How it was confirmed, with path:line where applicable.

review_limits.description: What this review could NOT establish: data not readable, pipeline not runnable, paper text unavailable, Stata semantics not verifiable by reading. Be explicit; silence here reads as false assurance.
